title: Senior Advertising Sales Manager, France (Paris based)
Senior Software Engineer - OpenCRQ
description_clean: 🌀 The CompanyFounded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity  shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future. 🎯 The RoleWe are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is curious about the modeling problem underneath cyber risk and wants to help shape a young product.You will join OpenCRQ as its fourth engineer and work across the data model, backend and product surface. Many foundations are still being defined, giving you meaningful influence beyond the features you directly own.You will shape these decisions with the squad and experienced engineering and product leaders across Filigran. We value constructive disagreement, clear reasoning and shared outcomes, and we expect everyone to ask for context, challenge assumptions and learn from one another.🧩 The problem you would be working onAsk a CISO what a cyber risk could cost, and the answer often still begins with a color: red, amber or green, often produced by a spreadsheet disconnected from current evidence.OpenCRQ replaces that color with a financial estimate and a traceable chain of evidence: which threat actors are active, which assets they can reach, which controls have proven effective and what the remaining exposure could cost.Every step is computed from live data and must withstand a simple question from a board: “Where does that figure come from?” That is what makes this an engineering problem rather than a reporting one.OpenCRQ is Filigran’s cyber risk quantification product. It combines threat intelligence from OpenCTI, exposure and control validation from OpenAEV, and agentic workflows through XTM One. As these products become more connected, the squad will define what agents can ask of the risk model, which evidence they can use and how their answers remain safe and explainable.🛠️ What you would work onEnd-to-end product ownership. Take product problems from early ideation and technical design through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. You will have the autonomy to drive the work, while using the squad to challenge assumptions and improve the outcome.The quantification engine. Turn threat frequency, control effectiveness and asset value into probabilistic loss distributions. Build general-purpose quantitative models that can evolve as assumptions and available evidence change, without losing reproducibility or explainability.The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation.Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain grows.The agentic surface. Design the contracts used by XTM One agents and the plain-language explanations behind risk figures. Together, the squad will define what models can safely do in a product whose outputs inform board-level decisions.🏆 What success could look likePriorities will evolve with the product, but within your first 6 to 12 months you could have:Taken a meaningful product problem from early ideation through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users.Shaped a core part of OpenCRQ’s interconnected data model or quantification engine and documented the trade-offs behind it.Made a major ingestion or calculation path more observable, recoverable and reproducible.Defined or implemented a durable contract between OpenCRQ and another Filigran product or an open standard, without making the internal model brittle.Helped ship risk results that users can trace back to the evidence that produced them.Contributed to the open-source release and to engineering practices the growing squad can build on.🌐 Open source, like the rest of FiligranOpenCRQ is about to become Open source, alongside OpenCTI and OpenAEV. You will contribute visibly to a product whose risk calculations can be inspected, challenged and improved by the organizations running it.👥 The squadYou will join two senior engineers and a staff engineer, reporting to OpenCRQ’s Engineering Manager. The squad is small enough for you to influence its direction, without working in isolation.You will collaborate with the VP of Technology, CTO and Principal Engineers on technical standards, and with the OpenCTI, OpenAEV and XTM One teams on cross-product contracts and integrations. These relationships bring domain knowledge and broader technical context into the squad’s decisions as it grows.✨ What will help you succeedWe do not expect you to arrive with expertise in cyber risk or every standard named below. We are looking for a strong software engineer who can learn quickly, work autonomously and use the squad to challenge and improve decisions.A track record of taking complex product problems from an ambiguous idea to a validated outcome: framing the problem, making technical decisions, implementing the solution, testing it end to end and checking that it solves the user’s need.Strong experience with a modern TypeScript stack and practical knowledge of PostgreSQL beyond the ORM. You treat failure modes and observability as part of the design.The ability to reason about complex relationships across systems and design interconnected data models that remain coherent as concepts and integrations evolve.Comfort turning quantitative concepts into maintainable software. Formal training in statistics is not required, but you should be willing to work with probability distributions, orders of magnitude and models whose assumptions evolve over time.Thoughtful use of coding agents: you know where they accelerate engineering and where their output needs careful verification.Fluent English is required.💡 Useful, but not requiredAny of the following would help, but none is expected:Experience in cybersecurity, GRC or risk quantification.Familiarity with STIX/TAXII, OCSF, MITRE ATT&CK or other open cybersecurity standards and frameworks.Experience shipping features involving LLM agents, RAG or MCP.⚙️ The stackTypeScript end to end: React, Vite and TanStack Router on the frontend; Node.js, Fastify and tRPC on the backend; PostgreSQL with a code-first schema and Drizzle, all in one monorepo.OpenCRQ ships as a container, both as SaaS and on customer-managed infrastructure. We use OpenTelemetry for traces, metrics and logs, alongside Prometheus and continuous profiling.A significant part of the design work happens at the boundaries between OpenCRQ, the rest of Filigran’s product suite and customer security tooling. You will work directly with the teams that own those systems rather than having to navigate those boundaries alone.🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job.We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company, and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation. You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.⭐ Be part of something biggerWe believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative.💻 Work at the edge of what’s nextWe bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice.🌍 Global opportunity without bordersBe part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us.🧭 A culture grounded in CORECohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity define how we work together — with openness, ownership, collaboration and respect. These are the principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people and grow together, especially when no one’s watching.💰 What you can expectCompetitive compensation + equity — everyone shares in our successRemote-first flexibility — work from wherever you’re based, with flexibility built into how we operate25 days PTO baseline — real time to disconnect, recharge and enjoy life outside workVolunteer days — paid time to contribute to causes that matter to youSet up for success — choose the equipment that works for you, with additional support for your remote work and development needs as our programs evolveTwo annual in-person get-togethers — one global company get-together and one team get-together, creating dedicated time to connect, collaborate and strengthen our culture beyond the screen🌍 Equal Employment OpportunityWe enable cybersecurity through inclusion — from code to culture.At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. description_clean:
Mindset
Chez Thiga, nous considérons qu’un Design System n’est pas seulement un ensemble de composants ou de règles : c’est un produit à part entière. Un produit pensé pour évoluer, répondre aux besoins des équipes, et accompagner la croissance de l’entreprise.
Créer et faire vivre un Design System demande une vision, une stratégie claire, et une gouvernance solide. Il faut piloter son adoption, anticiper ses usages à grande échelle, et s’assurer qu’il réponde aux enjeux à la fois du Design et de la Tech. C’est un levier puissant pour faire monter en maturité les organisations, structurer la collaboration entre les équipes, et diffuser une culture produit forte.
Aujourd'hui, un Design System bien structuré est aussi la condition sine qua non pour tirerpleinement parti de l'IA dans les workflows design et prototypage. Tokens cohérents,composants documentés, nomenclature rigoureuse autant de fondations qui permettentd'exploiter les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Lovable, v0...) de manière fiable et scalable.Le.la Design System Manager de demain est celui.celle qui anticipe ces usages et structure son système en conséquence.

How we get work done 🚀
Définir et piloter la roadmap du DS : feuille de route alignée sur les priorités produit et business, avec des objectifs mesurables à court et long terme.
Automatiser les workflows du DS au maximum : pipelines de tokens, synchronisation design to code en temps réel, scripts de génération de documentation, réduire au minimum les tâches manuelles et les risques de désynchronisation.
Structurer le DS pour l'IA et le prototypage rapide : concevoir une architecture de composants et de tokens qui rende le DS exploitable par les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Cursor, v0, Lovable...). Cela implique : nomenclature stricte,variantes bien définies, props documentées, et une logique de composants qui s'aligne avec les patterns du code.

description_clean: Über ValovaWir bauen die KI-Betriebsplattform für Europas Krankenhäuser, damit sich jede Ärztin und jeder Arzt auf die Patienten konzentrieren kann.Hinter jedem Fall steht eine Kette administrativer Aufgaben: Dokumentation, Kodierung, Abrechnung, Prüfungen, Planung. Sie läuft über getrennte Systeme und unzählige manuelle Übergaben, während die meisten deutschen Kliniken bereits rote Zahlen schreiben.Wir starten dort, wo der Effekt ab Tag eins messbar ist: vom Fall bis zum Geldeingang. Valova kodiert jeden Fall, verteidigt ihn in der Prüfung und sorgt dafür, dass das Geld ankommt. Von dort übernehmen wir jeden Workflow eines Krankenhauses, bis ein agentisches System die Routine erledigt und Menschen über Ausnahmen entscheiden. Erst Deutschland, dann Europa.Ein Team aus Ärzt:innen, Engineers, Strategieberater:innen und Start-up-Profis. Vor Ort in München und Berlin. Fachlich arbeitest Du eng mit unseren Kodier- und Abrechnungsexpert:innen: Sie kennen die Regeln, Du machst daraus Produkt. Du hast schon einmal ein Feature oder Projekt von der Idee bis zum Ergebnis verantwortet.Technisches Verständnis: Du musst nicht programmieren, kannst aber technische Dokumentation lesen und mit Engineers über Lösungen diskutieren.Präzises Denken: Du hinterfragst gern Prozesse und beschreibst Regeln so genau, dass Software sie umsetzen kann.Kommunikationsstärke: Du bist im Gespräch mit Ärzt:innen, Medizincontrolling und Technik gleichermaßen sicher.Reisebereitschaft: Du bist gern rund 20 bis 30 Prozent Deiner Zeit in Kliniken unterwegs.Sprachen: Du sprichst Deutsch fließend auf C1-Niveau und gutes Englisch.Ein Plus: Kenntnisse in Kodierung oder Abrechnung (z. B. DRG, OPS, GOÄ), Erfahrung mit KIS-Software (z. B. Orbis, SAP IS-H, i.s.h.med) oder Tools wie Jira und Figma sowie erste Erfahrung mit Datenanalyse (Excel, SQL) oder KI-Anwendungen.Dir fehlen ein oder zwei Punkte, aber Du bist überzeugt, die richtige Person für diese Rolle zu sein? title: Vertrieb Industriewasseraufbereitung (m/w/d)
description_clean:
Unser Kunde ist ein etabliertes und wachstumsstarkes Unternehmen in der Umweltbranche mit den Geschäftsbereichen Industriewassermanagement und Entsorgung & Verwertung. Als führender Anbieter für Betriebsführungs- und Betreiberlösungen in der industriellen Abwasseraufbereitung und Prozesswasserbehandlung bietet das Unternehmen ein breites Portfolio für das Wassermanagement in der produzierenden Industrie – von Betriebsführungskonzepten über Wartung und Instandhaltung bis hin zu eigenen Betriebschemikalien.
Wir suchen keine Verwalter – wir suchen echte Macher mit Vertriebsgen. Menschen, die Chancen erkennen, Verantwortung übernehmen und den Anspruch haben, beim Kunden wirklich etwas zu bewegen.
Das Unternehmen ist Teil einer international aufgestellten, vertikal integrierten Unternehmensgruppe mit rund 45 Gesellschaften und entsprechendem Zugang zu Infrastruktur, Technologie und Verwertungswegen sowie echten Wettbewerbsvorteilen im Markt.
Am Standort München oder in der Filiale in Offenbach an der Queich arbeitest du nah am Markt und übernimmst eine aktive Rolle im Ausbau des Geschäfts. Du bist nicht nur Ansprechpartner, sondern Treiber: Du erkennst Potenziale, entwickelst Lösungen und bringst sie beim Kunden auf die Straße. Dabei kannst du dich auf ein erfahrenes Team im Hintergrund verlassen, das dich operativ unterstützt.
Aufgaben

Du gewinnst neue Industrie- und Gewerbekunden für unsere Lösungen im Bereich Industriewasser, Abwasserbehandlung und Entsorgung und betreust den bestehenden Kundenstamm; dabei berätst du zu wasserwirtschaftlichen und abfalltechnischen Fragestellungen.
Du analysierst Kundenprozesse (z. B. Prozesswasser, Abwasserströme), bewertest Stoffströme und entwickelst passende Lösungen – von der Aufbereitung über Kreislaufführung bis zur Entsorgung.
Du erstellst Kalkulationen sowie Angebote und bringst technische Lösungen wirtschaftlich sauber auf den Punkt; Markt- und Wettbewerbsanalysen gehören ebenfalls zu deinem Aufgabengebiet.
Du verhandelst eigenverantwortlich Verträge, führst Preis- und Vertragsverhandlungen und schließt Verträge mit Neu- und Bestandskunden ab.
Du begleitest Projekte und Großaufträge, koordinierst interne Schnittstellen (Technik, Betrieb, Logistik) und stellst eine reibungslose Umsetzung sicher.
Du pflegst Kundendaten und Dokumentationen und stellst sicher, dass alle abfall- und wasserrechtlichen Vorschriften sowie Qualitätsrichtlinien eingehalten werden.
Du beobachtest den Markt, erkennst Trends im Bereich Industriewasser und Kreislaufwirtschaft und repräsentierst das Unternehmen auf Fachmessen.

Qualifikation

Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium oder Ausbildung in der Abfall-/Wasserwirtschaft, Verfahrenstechnik, Umwelttechnik, Chemie beziehungsweise eine vergleichbare kaufmännische oder technische Qualifikation. 
Erfahrung im Vertrieb von Entsorgungs-, Umwelt- oder wassertechnischen Dienstleistungen sowie in der Projektbegleitung; idealerweise auch Erfahrung in der Wasser- und Abwassertechnik oder der industriellen Prozesswasserbehandlung. 
Fundiertes Verständnis der Abfallwirtschaft, Kreislaufwirtschaft sowie grundlegender wasserwirtschaftlicher Prozesse; Fähigkeit, Stoffströme und Prozesszusammenhänge zu bewerten. 
Ausgeprägtes Kommunikations-, Verhandlungs- und Präsentationsgeschick. 
Selbstständige, strukturierte Arbeitsweise, Teamfähigkeit und sicherer Umgang mit MS-Office-Anwendungen. 
Erfahrung mit der Bestimmung der Trockensubstanzkonzentration (CTS) und Umgang mit entsprechenden Analyseverfahren ist ein Plus. 
Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und umgangssprachliche Englischkenntnisse.
Führerschein der Klasse B und Reisebereitschaft.

Benefits

Sicherer Arbeitsplatz in einer nachhaltigen Zukunftsbranche mit langfristiger Perspektive.
Transparente Vergütung mit erfolgsabhängiger Leistungsvergütung, Spesen und Corporate Benefits.
Dienstwagen zur privaten Nutzung inklusive Tankkarte.
Flexible Arbeitsmodelle mit Home‑Office‑Möglichkeit und familienfreundlichen Arbeitszeiten.
Intensive Einarbeitung und kontinuierliche Weiterbildungs‑ und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten.
Flache Hierarchien, ein motiviertes Team und Kommunikation auf Augenhöhe.

Fragen zur Position und zum Unternehmen beantwortet dir gerne Felix Wilhelm telefonisch oder per WhatsApp unter 0176 954 220 94. Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung (Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse, Gehaltsvorstellung, möglicher Eintrittstermin).Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (f/m/d)
description_clean: About ValovaWe are building the AI operations platform for European hospitals, so every clinician can focus on patients.Behind every patient sits a chain of admin work: documentation, coding, billing, audits, scheduling. It runs through disconnected systems and endless manual hand-offs, while most German hospitals already operate at a loss.We start where the impact is measurable from day one: case to cash. Valova codes every case, defends it in audits and makes sure the money lands. From there we take on every workflow that runs a hospital, until one agentic system handles the routine and people decide the exceptions. First Germany, then Europe.Doctors, engineers and operators, on-site in Munich and Berlin. Join us!Why this role mattersValova only works as well as it fits into the hospital. Our product creates the most value when it’s deeply connected to a hospital’s systems and built around how coders and medical controlling actually work. Today, connecting to a hospital information system can take months. That’s time hospitals keep losing revenue and coders keep working by hand.That’s where you come in. As Forward Deployed Engineer, you own technical go-lives from start to finish: from the first sandbox to production, from the interface to the workflow on the ward. You’re the bridge between hospital IT, the people who use Valova and our engineering team.Your impact is easy to see: in hospitals that go live faster, in integrations that run reliably, and in a product that gets better with every deployment because you bring back what you learn.This is a hands-on engineering role with real code in production and direct influence on our roadmap. It’s not a support desk, not a pre-sales role and not project management where others do the building. And it’s not a desk job: you’ll regularly be on site in hospitalsHow the role sits in the teamYou report directly to Christian, our CTO, and work day to day with our engineering team on connectors, deployments and internal tooling. With Malte and our product team, you turn what you see in hospitals into clear requirements. In hospital projects, you work hand in hand with our customer success and sales team and on the hospital side with IT leads, KIS vendors, coders and medical controlling.What you will doBring hospitals live: You take hospitals from sandbox to production, deploy Valova on hospital VMs and connect it to KIS systems such as SAP i.s.h.med, Orbis or Dedalus.Build the connections: You build and maintain interfaces (HL7, FHIR, archive and document exports) together with hospital IT and their partners.Set up Valova for each customer: You configure document types, case filtering, department rules and coding workflows.Learn from the ward: You work on site with coders and medical controlling and turn their friction into clear product requirements.Make deployments repeatable: You write the code that makes the next go-live faster: connectors, scripts, monitoring and internal tooling.Earn the hospital’s trust: You answer technical questions in security and data protection reviews (BSI C5, GDPR).What we are looking for:Engineering experience: At least two years in software engineering, and you’re comfortable with Linux, Docker and basic networking.Integration know-how: You’ve worked on system integrations. Experience with HL7/FHIR or SAP environments is a big plus.Customer focus: You enjoy working with customers and explain technical topics clearly to IT leads and coders alike.High ownership: You move things forward, even when three parties are involved.Travel: You’re happy to spend around 30 percent of your time at hospitals across Germany.Languages: You speak fluent German and English, since our customers work in German.Location: You work from our office in Munich or Berlin.Missing one or two points, but convinced you’re the right person for this role? Apply anyway. We’re looking forward to meeting you!What you getWork that means something, every day. Your agents are the core of our product and directly help improve the German healthcare system.Ownership from week one. You take over real projects with a clear outcome and your name on it, not a list of tasks someone else defined.Direct access to the founders. You work day to day with our founders Sophia, a physician and ex-McKinsey consultant, and Christian, who has founded two health tech startups and spent a decade building clinical systems. No layers, no waiting weeks for approvals.Trust and freedom. We trust you to solve problems your way, and the team has your back 100%.Learning at startup speed. You will see more in one year here than in three years elsewhere, across models, infrastructure, product and customers, with a team that has a proven track record of deploying AI in healthcare.One team, in the heart of the city. We work together on-site at WeWork Odeonsplatz in Munich and WeWork in central Berlin. Fully serviced offices with coffee, meeting rooms and phone booths mean zero admin, and the city-center location means short commutes, easy access to customers and investors, and lunch spots around every corner.Team events that bring Munich and Berlin together, because the people you build with should also be the people you celebrate with.What success looks likeAfter 3 months, you know Valova’s stack inside out and have taken a hospital through its first technical setup together with our team.After 6 months, you’ve taken at least two hospitals live, and a new KIS connection takes weeks instead of months.After 12 months, our deployments are largely repeatable: connectors, scripts and monitoring you built make every go-live faster.Throughout, what you learn in hospitals shapes our roadmap, and hospital IT teams see you as their trusted contact at Valova.How it worksJust upload your CV with your application. We’ll get in touch with you for the next steps:Intro call (30 min): We get to know each other, talk about your background and answer your first questions.Technical interview with Christian (CTO) (60 min): We dive into your engineering experience and the integrations you’ve built.Case: You work through a realistic hospital integration scenario and present it to the team.References: We speak with two or three people you’ve worked with, such as former managers or colleagues.Meet the team: You spend a day with us on-site in Munich or Berlin, meet our founders Sophia and Christian and see how we work day to day.Offer: If it’s a match for both sides, you’ll hear from us quickly.We look forward to your application, regardless of gender, background, religion, disability, age or sexual identity.Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

About us
We love pets - which is why we're on a mission to make the world a better place for pets and their parents.  We offer pet insurance policies with generous pet health benefits that are designed with their needs in mind. We've helped half a million pets stay happy and healthy since 2017 - and many more customers throughout the world are joining us every day.  Our company is respectful, fun-loving and passionate about pets and their wellbeing.  Throughout our business you'll meet people who think differently, aim for impact, and love to try new things.  Want to join our pack?  Join us. Love every moment. Love ManyPets. 
A day in the life
As a Platform Engineer, you will initially join our platform squad. We build and maintain the AWS infrastructure, deployment pipelines, tooling and engineering standards that every other squad at ManyPets depends on.
This role has a strong security focus, and it will become more security focused over time. Much of the work is compliance and assurance: building and running the tooling that checks our cloud estate against our security standards, writing the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one, gathering the evidence we need for ISO 27001 and our other obligations, and supporting the audits that depend on it. Alongside that you will help us tighten access controls across our cloud estate, and take on ownership of the edge and network security tooling that protects our services.
Over time this role moves across to work directly with our Head of Security as we build out a dedicated security function at ManyPets. You will help shape what that function does and how it works, rather than inheriting something already built.
Our environment is fast-paced and highly collaborative. You will work closely with your teammates using pair or mob programming, participating in regular workshops and planning sessions, primarily over Zoom, with occasional in-person collaboration.
We embrace modern development practices:
· All our services are cloud-hosted on AWS, using serverless and event-driven architectures for scalability and resilience.
· We use a fully automated deployment pipeline, allowing you to release to production within minutes, multiple times per day.
· We define our infrastructure as code, and we emphasise observability, testing and secure-by-design principles from the start.
As a squad we own our work end-to-end, including development, maintenance and support. You will play a key role in ensuring the reliability and quality of what we provide to the rest of engineering, and contribute to a culture of rapid learning and continuous improvement.
Your responsibilities
ü Build and maintain secure platform foundations
o Design, build and maintain the shared cloud infrastructure, tooling and deployment pipelines that other squads rely on.
o Define infrastructure as code so our environments are consistent, repeatable and reviewable.
o Make secure configuration the default, so squads get it without having to ask for it.
o Maintain the edge and network security tooling that protects our services.
o Share in the day-to-day operational ownership of the platform, responding to requests and issues raised by other squads.
 
Make our security posture measurable
o Automate the gathering of evidence for ISO 27001 and our other compliance obligations, so that an audit means pulling a report rather than running a manual exercise.
o Write the scripts and small services that turn a manual security check into a scheduled, repeatable one.
o Triage findings from our scanning and posture tooling such as Aikido and Ascidian, work out which ones actually matter, and either fix them or get them in front of the team that can.
o Work with our Head of Security to turn written policy into controls that are enforced by tooling.
 
Strengthen access and identity controls
o Review and tighten access across our cloud accounts, working towards least privilege.
o Improve how we manage secrets, credentials and machine identities.
o Make access changes auditable, and straightforward for engineers to request and for us to review.
 
Extend our platform standards beyond AWS
o Help us apply the standards, tooling and controls we have built in AWS to our Google Cloud estate.
o Work with the teams who use Google Cloud to understand their needs and where the gaps are.
 
Team collaboration
o Work closely with other squad members and stakeholders to align on goals and solutions.
o Support engineers across other squads who use our platform, and take their feedback seriously.
o Proactively build shared understanding across the team through pairing, discussions, and reviews.
o Document your work clearly to support knowledge sharing and future maintenance.
 
Self development
o Take ownership of your learning journey and technical development plan.
o Approach challenges with curiosity and a growth mindset.
o Learn from your peers and actively seek feedback and mentorship.
 
Your skills and experience
We are looking for someone with:
· Commercial experience building and maintaining cloud infrastructure on a major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud or Azure).
· Hands-on experience defining infrastructure as code.
· Experience building and maintaining continuous integration and deployment pipelines.
· A good working understanding of cloud security fundamentals.
· Proficiency in at least one scripting language, ideally Python.
· Comfort working in a regulated environment. We are FCA regulated and take our ISO 27001 commitments seriously.
 
You will also need at least one current associate-level cloud certification:
· AWS: Solutions Architect Associate, Developer Associate or SysOps Administrator Associate. We would also be interested in the AWS Certified Security Speciality.
· Google Cloud: Associate Cloud Engineer.
· Microsoft Azure: Administrator Associate (AZ-104) or Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500).
 
Entry-level certifications such as AWS Cloud Practitioner, Google Cloud Digital Leader and Azure Fundamentals do not meet this on their own. Please include the certification name and your credential ID or badge link with your application.
 
We would also like to see at least one of the following. You do not need both, and we will support you to build the other:
· A security specialism, where you can tell us about security or compliance tooling you have built and what it caught.
· Experience across more than one cloud provider, ideally both AWS and Google Cloud.
The interview process
This position has a four-stage interview process, which will be held via Zoom.
· Stage 1 - an initial conversation with a member of our Talent team.
· Stage 2 - an informal meeting with the hiring manager for about 45 minutes. We will explain more about the role and explore how your experience matches up with what we need.
· Stage 3 - a longer interview, up to an hour, with the hiring manager and two engineers from the team. We will ask some competency questions and work through a technical scenario together. There is no take-home exercise.
· Stage 4 - an informal conversation with our Head of Security.
About the team
The EPD ("Engineering, Product and Design") team operates with a squad system and Agile ways of working within quarterly terms - and we really enjoy working collaboratively. We hold regular 'Hack Weeks' to look at products and address problems relating to the business, and we get the chance to highlight and work on things we're interested in and feel passionately about.
Our tech stack
We are on a mission to become the best we can be, constantly challenging ourselves to achieve and learn. You will be supported to learn new technology – both in breadth and depth - and encouraged to challenge our ways of thinking with new and innovative ideas.
Our "north star" is to become an elite performer as defined by the 4 key DORA metrics. To drive towards elite status, we apply and continually inspect and adapt the best Agile frameworks and practices inspired by DevOps, SRE, Scrum, XP and Lean. We are a highly collaborative environment and regularly practice Mob and Pair based programming which we believe improve our quality of delivery and share understanding.
We take our operational performance, security, and reliability as seriously as our quality and development practices. We are cloud hosted and highly automated, primarily on AWS with some critical services running on Google Cloud.
Some specific technologies we use include: AWS | Google Cloud | Python | MongoDB | Aikido | Ascidian | Cloudflare
 Salary range:£55,000—£65,000 GBPWays of working
On a typical day you'll be working from a laptop with a screen, mouse, keyboard, and headset.  You'll be meeting your colleagues on Zoom and keeping in touch regularly via email and Slack too – we'd expect you to be using your computer for around seven hours a day.  We'd ask that you have a distraction-free work area and a reliable internet connection with a speed of 25Mbps so you can work effectively.  We'll make sure you have the right home set-up that supports you in the role by providing best-in-class technology, money towards a desk, and vision support.
Inclusion at ManyPets
We promise to give you the same opportunities as everyone else and we won't discriminate against you at any point in the process. This includes how we source talent, our interview process, our conditions of employment (including pay) and feedback.  If you'd like to read more about this, please download our Approach to Inclusion policy.

description_clean: Mines Saint-Etienne est une Ecole de l’Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT), 1er groupe public d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management en France. L’IMT est un EPSCP (grand établissement) sous la tutelle du Ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique.L’École Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Saint-Étienne (Mines Saint-Etienne) est chargée de missions de formation, de recherche et d’innovation, de transfert vers l’industrie et de culture scientifique, technique et industrielle.Mines Saint-Etienne représente: 2 400 élèves-ingénieurs et chercheurs en formation, 480 personnels (150 Chercheurs et Enseignants-chercheurs), un budget consolidé de 46 M€, 3 campus dédiés à l’industrie à Saint-Etienne et Lyon (région AURA), à la microélectronique et aux objets connectés à Gardanne (Métropole Aix-Marseille Provence, région SUD) et à l’ingénierie pour la santé à Saint-Etienne ; 6 unités de recherche ; 5 centres de formation et de recherche ; un centre de culture scientifique technique et industrielle leader en France « La Rotonde » (> 50 000 visiteurs / an). Contexte scientifique et objectifs du stage :Des dispositifs d’électronique organique ultra-flexibles, conformables et implantables incorporant une intelligence artificielle promettent de révolutionner la surveillance et le traitement en temps réel de maladies chroniques [1]. De tels systèmes pourraient être basés sur des transistors organiques électrochimiques (OECTs), exploitant des conducteurs polymères mixtes ion-électron (PMIECs) comme couches actives. En effet, les PMIECs sont apparus comme une excellente plateforme matérielle pour interfacer la biologie avec l’électronique conventionnelle ; identifié comme le domaine de la « bioélectronique organique ou plastique ». L’OECT est considéré comme l’éléments clé pour réaliser une telle interface [2]. Son efficacité est évaluée suivant des figures de mérite (FoMs) telles que i) la transconductance (gm), et/ou ii) les temps de commutation (ionique vs. électronique) dans le dispositif. Au-delà des applications de transduction, à court terme, l’OECT est aussi intéressant pour créer des applications émergentes en matière de circuits neuromorphiques bioélectroniques [3].La réalisation de tels circuits est freinée par un manque de compréhension et d’optimisation des processus de conduction mixte dans ces matériaux polymériques ; notamment une asymétrie des temps de commutation des transistors lors des séquences de dopage (i.e « ON ») vs dédopage (i.e « OFF ») dans le canal de l’OECT. Des outils de caractérisation in-situ & operando permettant de quantifier et cartographier les paramètres de transduction électronique et électrochimique dans le canal de l’OECT se révèlent être indispensables pour comprendre les limitations actuelles en performances des PMIECs et/ou pour construire des PMIECs optimums dans de tels circuits neuromorphiques. Dans ce contexte scientifique, le.la stagiaire développera une nouvelle mesure de spectroscopie et instrumentation d’optique non linéaire, appelée microscopie par génération de second harmonique résolue en temps, afin d’enregistrer le mouvement spatio-temporel des espèces chargées, ion et électrons (ou trous), et ainsi donc cartographier les mobilités électroniques in-situ & operando le canal de l’OECT.La.le stagiaire fabriquera ces dispositifs OECTs en salle blanche de microélectronique, et bénéficiera d’un accompagnement technique pour leur réalisation. Il.elle enregistrera et analysera les FoMs clés grâce à l'expérimentation d’optique non linéaire développée et aux caractérisations électriques et électrochimiques afin d’établir, de manière plus globale, des règles d’ingénierie dans ces PMIECs qui serviront de socle de connaissances incontournables à l’avenir, pour mettre en œuvre et appliquer des circuits neuromorphiques à base d'OECTs, comme première brique d’une intelligence artificielle d’électronique organique. Pour aller plus loin :[1] https://iconic.mines-stetienne.fr/[2] https://doi.org/10.1038/ s43586-021-00065-8[3] https://www.nature.com/articles/s41578-023-00622-5🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vousLa candidate ou le candidat devra être en cours de formation et d’apprentissage d’un diplôme de Master 2 ou de 3ème année de diplôme d’ingénieurs en Techniques Optiques et Instrumentations. title: CENTRALE LYON - PhD Silicon Photonics for Scalable Energy-Efficient AI Hardware Accelerators
description_clean: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) applications across cloud and edge environments is driving the need for highly efficient hardware capable of supporting increasingly demanding workloads. Among these, matrix multiplication – particularly General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) – remains the dominant computational kernel in modern AI models, including deep neural networks and transformer architectures. Conventional electronic accelerators, while highly optimized, face growing challenges related to energy consumption, data movement, and scalability. Silicon photonics has emerged as a promising technology to address these limitations by enabling highbandwidth, low-latency, and potentially energy-efficient computation through optical signal processing. In particular, recent advances in photonic computing leveraging phase-change materials (PCM) offer new opportunities for implementing reconfigurable and non-volatile computational primitives directly in the optical domain. This PhD is part of the CAMELIA program (ASIC and Numérique agencies) within the targeted project LEAF, and aims to explore a hybrid photonic–electronic computing paradigm for AI acceleration. The central objective is to design and evaluate silicon photonics-based architectures for efficient GEMM operations, building on recent work demonstrating a reconfigurable photonic GEMM architecture based on PCM and stochastic computing. The proposed research will focus on extending this tile-based photonic GEMM approach toward large-scale matrix operations under realistic conditions. Key challenges include managing PCM-related constraints such as limited precision and quantization effects, mitigating noise and variability, and addressing interface latency between photonic and electronic domains. A major aspect of the PhD will be the development of system-level evaluation and benchmarking methodologies within a design-technology co-optimization (DTCO/SDTCO) framework. The objective is to provide quantitative and objective metrics for decision-making, including scalability analysis, computational throughput, and energy efficiency for target AI workloads. These evaluations will support both intermediate design exploration and the potential experimental validation of fabricated demonstrators within the broader program. In addition, the PhD will address electronic circuit design challenges associated with photonic accelerators, including interface circuits for control, programming of PCM elements, optical-to-electrical readout, and signal conversion. These aspects are critical for ensuring the practical integration of photonic computing units within heterogeneous AI hardware systems. The expected outcome is a set of novel architectures, models, and evaluation tools that will clarify the potential and limitations of silicon photonics for next-generation AI accelerators, and provide guidelines for scalable and energy-efficient implementations.  Background: The candidate should hold or be about to obtain an MSc in Electronics Engineering, Photonics, or Computer Engineering. A strong background in computer architecture, integrated circuits, or photonic systems is expected. Knowledge of AI hardware accelerators, in-memory computing, or silicon photonics will be appreciated. Environment: The PhD will be carried out at the INL laboratory, within the CAMELIA program, as part of the LEAF project, in collaboration between leading academic and institutional partners in AI hardware and photonics. title: Chief Customer Officer
description_clean:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 
Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank. We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.
Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job. We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow. We are committed to changing the way things are done.
Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position Work from anywhere!Position overview
Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 
Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.
The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.
The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.
This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.
The mandate

 Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
 Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would. You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
 Win the right members, efficiently. You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
 Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances. Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
 Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless. You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most.  Build one Customer organisation, not four. Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
 Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call. You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate
This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done 

10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).

Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.
What this role is not

Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.

Je combineert technische analyses met advies en vertaalt complexe vraagstukken naar veilige, uitvoerbare en duurzame oplossingen. Daarbij werk je nauw samen met opdrachtgevers en collega's. Binnen het team deel je jouw expertise en begeleid je, afhankelijk van je ervaring, ook junior adviseurs inhoudelijk.Dit ben jij bij MovaresJe bent een ervaren geotechnisch adviseur die verder kijkt dan zijn eigen berekening. Je overziet het geheel, maakt inhoudelijke keuzes en weet collega’s daarin mee te nemen. Je vindt het leuk om kennis te delen en bij te dragen aan de ontwikkeling van collega’s en het team. Werk je nu bij een gespecialiseerd bureau en mis je de breedte van projecten, de invloed op inhoudelijke keuzes of de ruimte om collega’s te begeleiden? Of wil je jouw geotechnische expertise inzetten in projecten met grote maatschappelijke impact? Dan past deze rol goed bij jou.Dit breng je ook mee:meerdere jaren ervaring binnen de geotechniek, passend bij een medior- of seniorrol; ervaring met Deltares-software (D-serie); ervaring met Plaxis is een pre, net zoals affiniteit met lijninfrastructuur;sterke schriftelijke en mondelinge vaardigheden in zowel het Nederlands als Engels. Dit krijg je bij MovaresBij Movares werk je aan opgaven die Nederland verder helpen. Tegelijk krijg je de ruimte om je werk en loopbaan in te richten op een manier die bij jou past. Met goede arbeidsvoorwaarden, veel flexibiliteit en volop mogelijkheden om je te ontwikkelen.Een sterk fundamentEen goede basis begint bij voorwaarden waarop je kunt rekenen:een salaris tussen € 4.650 en € 7.580 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur;een flexibele pot van minimaal 15% van je jaarsalaris, inclusief vakantiegeld;een goede pensioenregeling bij Zwitserleven, waarbij Movares twee derde van de pensioenpremie betaalt;een NS Business Card voor woon-werkverkeer en zakelijke reizen. Privé profiteer je met de kaart van de dalurenkorting.Maximaal flexibelVorm een manier van werken die aansluit bij jouw leven én jouw ambities. Maak keuzes die bij jou passen:flexibel werken volgens ons Any Time Any Place-principe, passend bij je team, klanten en projecten;De mogelijkheid om twee weken per jaar te werken vanaf je vakantieadres binnen de EU;20 vakantiedagen bij een fulltime dienstverband, met de mogelijkheid om extra dagen te kopen vanuit je flexibele pot;met je flexibele pot kies je wat voor jou belangrijk is, bijvoorbeeld voor extra inkomen, pensioen, een fiets, bedrijfsfitness, verduurzaming van je woning of het aflossen van je studieschuld;€ 750 budget per vijf jaar om je thuiswerkplek goed in te richten;€ 2,45 netto thuiswerkvergoeding per thuiswerkdag.Veel ontwikkelmogelijkhedenOntwikkel een loopbaan die past bij jouw talenten en ambities. Kies jouw eigen pad:ruimte om je expertise, ambitie en loopbaan verder te ontwikkelen;leren door te doen, samen met ervaren collega's en met gebruik van een breed aanbod aan ontwikkelmogelijkheden;de kans om actief kennis te delen en mee te bouwen aan de toekomst van ons vakgebied.Samen groeienDeel mee in de waarde die we samen creëren en de groei van onze organisatie. Samen voor succes:je flexibele pot groeit mee met de resultaten van Movares;een winstdeling met een doelbedrag van 5% van je brutojaarsalaris, afhankelijk van de resultaten;en de mogelijkheid tot participeren in de waardeontwikkeling van Movares door middel van aankoop van phantom-aandelen.Jouw team bij MovaresJe werkt samen met een hechte groep geotechnische adviseurs die elkaar makkelijk weten te vinden. Eén dag per week – op woensdag – werken jullie sowieso samen op kantoor in Utrecht. Daarnaast is twee dagen per week op kantoor gangbaar, maar stemmen we locatie en werktijden flexibel af. Er is altijd iemand aanwezig en de lijnen zijn kort.De sfeer in het team is open en gelijkwaardig. Er is weinig hiërarchie: senioriteit gaat hier niet over ‘boven iemand staan’, maar over kennis delen en elkaar verder helpen. Collega’s kunnen goed met elkaar opschieten, schakelen snel en staan voor elkaar klaar. Samenwerken doen we bewust, omdat we geloven dat je daar betere oplossingen van maakt. title: Ontwikkelaar vastgoed
description_clean: Wil jij bouwen aan de vastgoedopgave én aan een nieuwe ontwikkelorganisatie? Als ervaren ontwikkelaar bij Dura Vermeer Bouw & Vastgoed werk je aan grootschalige vastgoedprojecten in Midden-Nederland. Je stapt in na acquisitie en bent verantwoordelijk voor de verdere ontwikkeling richting verkoop en realisatie. In een ondernemende omgeving krijg je alle ruimte om mee te bouwen aan het team, je expertise in te zetten in de samenwerking met adviseurs én door te groeien naar een rol met meer inhoudelijke en coachende verantwoordelijkheid. Dit wordt jouw baanOndernemend, ervaren en klaar om impact te maken? Dan voel jij je thuis binnen deze nieuwe ontwikkelorganisatie van Dura Vermeer. Als senior Projectontwikkelaar werk je aan omvangrijke vastgoedprojecten en help je niet alleen projecten verder te brengen, maar ook het team en de organisatie. Je begrijpt hoe ontwikkeling en bouw elkaar versterken, neemt eigenaarschap en krijgt de ruimte om mee te denken, mee te bouwen en mee te groeien. Je bent betrokken vanaf de fase na acquisitie / tendergunning en schakelt intensief met de het ontwikkelteam om projecten succesvol verder te brengen. Wat ga je doenDe focus ligt op het moment waarop een tender is gewonnen of een acquisitie is verworven en projecten daadwerkelijk ontwikkeld gaan worden. Je werkt aan (middel)grote vastgoedontwikkelingen en ben je de verbindende factor tussen ontwikkeling en bouw. Dat maakt deze rol ideaal voor een ervaren ontwikkelaar die energie krijgt van het uitwerken van projecten, ondernemerschap toont en wil meegroeien met een ambitieuze organisatie.·       Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de ontwikkeling van woningbouwprojecten vanaf tendergunning/acquisitie, naar omgevingsvergunning tot aan de start van de verkoop;·       Je bewaakt de businesscase en stuurt op waardecreatie gedurende het gehele ontwikkelproces;·       Je vertaalt ambities en plannen naar concrete ontwikkelbeslissingen die bijdragen aan een succesvolle uitvoering;·       Je stuurt het ontwikkelproces aan op het gebied van kwaliteit, planning, financiën en risico's;·       Je verbindt de belangen van gemeenten, adviseurs, beleggers, corporaties, bouwteams en andere stakeholders;·       Je werkt intensief samen met collega's van Bouw om projecten optimaal uitvoerbaar en haalbaar te maken;·       Je werkt nauw samen met makelaars, verkoopmanagers en notarissen om projecten succesvol in verkoop te brengen;·       Je voert regie op vergunningstrajecten, overeenkomsten en besluitvorming;·       Je draagt actief bij aan de verdere opbouw en professionalisering van de ontwikkelorganisatie.Meer bij Dura VermeerDura Vermeer is een onafhankelijk familiebedrijf. En dat merk je. In hoe we samenwerken, naar elkaar omkijken en bouwen met oog voor de volgende generaties. Al sinds 1855 bouwen we aan Nederland, in woningbouw, utiliteitsbouw, infrastructuur en techniek. Onze onafhankelijkheid en lange termijn visie vormen daarbij de basis.Met een omzet van € 2,6 miljard en ruim 3.700 collega’s behoren we tot de top van de Nederlandse bouwsector. Maar uiteindelijk draait het bij ons niet om die cijfers. Het draait om mensen. Om collega’s die samen werken aan projecten waar je trots op bent iconisch én dichtbij en bijdragen aan oplossingen voor maatschappelijke vraagstukken.Onze ambities zijn groot. En die maken we alleen waar met betrokken mensen. Daarom investeren we in goed werkgeverschap en een werkomgeving waarin jij je thuis voelt. Waar je jezelf kunt zijn, je veilig voelt en je uitspreekt. Zodat jij het beste uit jezelf haalt en samen met ons meer maakt.Hier zit je op jouw plekBij Dura Vermeer Bouw en Vastgoed Utrecht staan we aan het begin van een nieuw hoofdstuk. Waar we jarenlang bekend stonden als een sterke renovatie/transformatiespecialist, zijn we sinds begin dit jaar uitgegroeid tot een volwaardige Bouw en Vastgoed organisatie. Naast renovatie en transformatie realiseren we nu ook nieuwbouwprojecten in de woning- en utiliteitsbouw én zetten we de volgende stap naar eigen gebieds- en vastgoedontwikkeling.Dat betekent dat je terechtkomt in een organisatie die volop in beweging is. Met ruim 100 collega's binnen onze werkmaatschappij bouwen we niet alleen aan duurzame woningen, utiliteitsprojecten en leefomgevingen, maar ook aan de toekomst van onze eigen organisatie. De lijnen zijn kort, de ambities groot en de kansen om mee te bouwen aan nieuwe werkwijzen, teams en projecten liggen voor het oprapen.Hier krijg je de ruimte om impact te maken. Niet vanaf de zijlijn, maar midden in een frisse organisatie die zich verder ontwikkelt en waarin ondernemerschap, samenwerking en eigenaarschap centraal staan. Samen bouwen we aan projecten waar we trots op zijn én aan een organisatie die klaar is voor de toekomst. Je komt het beste tot je recht wanneer met alle betrokken partijen, de complexe projecten succesvol weet te ontwikkelen én realiseren.Dit bieden wij jouHet salaris voor deze functie ligt bij senior profiel tussen € 6.512,- en € 9.512,- (op basis van 40 uur), exclusief 8% vakantiegeld. title: Data Analyst
description_clean: Help launch our new temping product and drive commercial impact!At YoungOnes, data is at the start of every decision. Our Data & RevOps team has a seat at every table and takes a leading role in where the company goes next. Two years ago we rebuilt our data environment in Databricks from scratch, and it is fully ready for the future. There are few better environments to work in.We are looking for a Data Analyst with a focus on product, who also supports our marketing and commercial teams with deeper analyses. Someone with experience who is ready to take responsibility, and who does not stop at a report but actively steers on the outcome.What will you do?Your main focus is product. Next to that, you support marketing and the commercial teams, which keeps your work varied.ProductIn the flexible work market, companies used to choose between temping (uitzenden) and freelancers. Since last year we have been bringing a new proposition to market that sits in between: non-service temping. It combines the legal certainty of temping with the flexibility and personal control of freelancing, all through our platform. This is an important step in our strategy towards one app for work.Take the lead in tracking the progress of this new proposition;Define the KPIs and funnel that show whether the proposition is working;Analyse the full journey of workers and clients, from onboarding to repeat shifts;Spot problems early and actively steer where you see them;Translate insights into concrete improvements together with product and development;Work in a select team that operates as a startup within the company.Commercial & marketing supportNext to product, you are the analytical sparring partner for our commercial teams and marketing. title: QA Engineer
description_clean: About the roleAt YoungOnes, you make sure our platform delivers on its promise: stable, reliable and free of surprises for the people who use it every day. As a QA Engineer you don't work at the end of the chain, but right in the middle of our development teams. You think along before any code is written, test smartly where it matters, and act as the bridge between development, product and the rest of the company when it comes to quality. You report to the Teamlead Frontend and work daily with the frontend, mobile and backend teams.What you'll doThink along from the start. You join refinements and help teams see the risks and impact of a feature before they start building;Choose the right test approach. Together with the team, you decide per feature what to test automatically, what to test manually, and why;Build and maintain automated tests. You set up tests for key platform functionality and keep them reliable;Manual and exploratory testing. You go through the app yourself, look for edge cases and find what a script misses;Central point of contact for bugs. Bug reports from across the company come to you. title: PR Teamlead (m/w/d)
description_clean:
Overview
PR steht vor einem strukturellen Bruch. Vertrauen verschiebt sich, Sichtbarkeit wird neu verteilt, KI wächst exponentiell. Wir bei getpress glauben, dass Reputation in den nächsten zehn Jahren der entscheidende Wettbewerbsvorsprung für Unternehmen wird.
Deshalb bauen wir die PR Company der Zukunft. Outcome-getrieben statt Retainer-Stunden. KI-first statt KI-on-top. Automatisiert, wo es skaliert und menschlich, wo es wirklich zählt. Unser über 40-köpfiges Team aus Journalist*innen und PR-Strateg*innen hat seit 2017 die PR für 450+ der spannendsten Wachstumsunternehmen Europas gesteuert – und will mehr.  
Als PR Teamlead bist du nicht nur senior in deiner eigenen PR-Expertise, sondern gibst dein Wissen weiter, entwickelst erfahrene PR-Köpfe und Nachwuchstalente und trägst Verantwortung für ein wachsendes Kundenportfolio.
Bist du dabei?
Deine Rolle
Als Teamlead arbeitest du nicht mehr selbst operativ auf Kund*innen, sondern ausschließlich über dein Team – dein Impact entsteht durch gute Führung, nicht durch eigene Pitches.  

Teamentwicklung: Du bist Vorbild und Fels in der Brandung. Mit weekly 1:1s, regelmäßigen Feedbackgesprächen und individuellen Entwicklungsplänen erkennst du Stärken und Entwicklungspotenziale. Du entwickelst deine Teammitglieder individuell, vom Junior bis zum Senior.
Kundenportfolio: Du hast den Überblick über den Status aller Kund*innen im Team, bist strategische Ansprechperson auf Entscheiderebene und erkennst frühzeitig Risiken, ebenso wie Upsell-Potenziale und Wachstumschancen. So sorgst du langfristig für ein gesundes Portfolio in deinem Team.
Unternehmerisches Handeln: Dein Team ist eine kleine unternehmerische Einheit innerhalb von getpress: Du triffst strategische Entscheidungen auf Basis von KPIs und steuerst Team- und Kundenplanung. Dabei bist du nicht scheu, Entscheidungen zu treffen, zu priorisieren und zu delegieren.
Sales & Recruiting: Du arbeitest punktuell eng mit dem Sales-Team zusammen, etwa bei Neukund*innenpitches. Genauso eng arbeitest du mit People & Culture zusammen, wenn es um Mitarbeiterentwicklung, Onboarding und Recruiting geht.
Struktur & Qualität: Du baust Prozesse, die dein Team wirklich braucht, basierend auf den Bedürfnissen, die du erkennst. Du sorgst für gemeinsame Routinen, begleitest das Onboarding und trägst die Verantwortung für die Qualitätssicherung im Team.

Wer du bist

Du bringst über 4 Jahre Erfahrung in der operativen PR mit (idealerweise im Agenturumfeld) und hast selbst Kund*innen aus dem Mittelstand und vergleichbaren Unternehmensgrößen direkt betreut, weiterentwickelt und nachweislich in deutschen Leit- und Fachmedien platziert. Diese Erfahrung ist deine Basis.
Du hast bereits ein Team geführt und weiterentwickelt, disziplinarisch wie fachlich. Idealerweise hast du schon Change-Prozesse begleitet und weißt, wie man ein Team sicher durch Phasen des Wandels führt.
Du bringst erprobte Führungsskills, eine hohe emotionale Intelligenz und ein ehrliches Interesse für Menschen und ihre Entwicklung mit.
Du denkst unternehmerisch und hast ein ausgeprägtes Verständnis für Geschäftsstrategien. KPIs nutzt du bewusst und regelmäßig, um daraus strategische Entscheidungen abzuleiten.
Du bist Kommunikator*in durch und durch – im Team hörst du zu und nimmst Menschen mit; extern kommunizierst du souverän mit Kund*innen und Stakeholdern über Hierarchieebenen hinweg, vom CEO bis zum Marketing-Ansprechpartner.
Der Einsatz von KI in der PR-Arbeit ist für dich gelebter Alltag, keine Theorie. Du bist neugierig, testest aus, was möglich ist und teilst dein Wissen im Team.
Du sprichst Deutsch auf C2-Niveau, kannst auch auf Englisch professionell kommunizieren und lebst in Deutschland.

Was dich erwartet

Echte PR-Arbeit. Bei uns geht es um echte Pressearbeit, individuell und zielgerichtet. Keine Standard-Pressemitteilungen, sondern individuelles Pitchen bei Journalist*innen in einer breiten Range an Medien.
Optimismus. Wir glauben, dass man aus Fehlern lernt und dass eine optimistische Grundhaltung den Unterschied macht. Das merkt man nicht nur in unserem Daily Doing, sondern auch bei spontanen Coffee-Talks oder unseren regelmäßigen Teamevents, ob digital oder vor Ort.
Impact. Wir haben hohe Standards an unsere eigene Arbeit, aber auch an die Unternehmen, mit denen wir zusammenarbeiten. Vor allem in Europa gibt es mehr Hidden Champions als sichtbare Erfolgsgeschichten. Das ist die Lücke, die wir schließen wollen.
Sparring. Du stehst nie alleine da: Regelmäßiges Sparring gehört bei uns zum Alltag. Mit deiner eigenen Führungskraft, unserer Head of PR, ebenso wie mit anderen Teamleads, dem C-Level oder People & Culture, je nachdem, welches Thema gerade ansteht.
Perspektive. Auch als Teamlead lernt man nicht aus. Wir planen langfristig und wollen deine persönliche Entwicklung fördern. Du startest mit einem unbefristeten Arbeitsvertrag, und mit unserem Wachstum wächst auch der Raum, dein Wissen einzubringen und mit uns zu lernen. Etwa indem du uns bei Projekten oder der Entwicklung neuer Services unterstützt.
Flexibilität. Wir arbeiten hybrid, remote (in DE) oder im Office. Wir haben zwar Kernerreichbarkeitszeiten, aber wann du arbeitest, entscheidest du abgestimmt auf die Bedürfnisse von Team und Kund*innen. Vertrauen, Eigenständigkeit und Kommunikation sind für uns das A und O und sorgen dafür, dass wir Job und Privatleben gut miteinander vereinen können.
Benefits und Sweet Treats. Du kannst aus drei frei wählbaren Sachbezügen wählen, von einer betrieblichen Altersvorsorge mit 20% Zuschuss auf deine Einzahlungen profitieren, 180 Tage im Jahr aus dem EU-Ausland arbeiten, dich auf regelmäßige Teamevents freuen. Und das Beste: Du startest mit 27 Urlaubstagen, aber je länger du bei uns bist, desto mehr Urlaubstage bekommst du dazu.

Wie gehts weiter?
Wenn du jetzt denkst: ,,Klingt nach mir!'', dann bewirb dich ohne Anschreiben bei uns und wer weiß, vielleicht bist du schon schneller als gedacht Teil unseres getpress-Teams!Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

Typische Tickets?
1st Level Support

We proudly support 2,400 customers in 64 countries, with 80% of our clientele comprising listed companies in major markets such as Europe, North America, and the Middle East. 


Our Recognition: 


DiliTrust has been at the forefront of Legal Tech innovation, being the first Legal Tech with AI features since 2022. The company is renowned for providing a positive and entrepreneurial work environment. We are honored to have received the "Happy at Work" and "Tech at Work" labels every year since 2019. 




The Role:


Lini is DiliTrust's proprietary AI engine, powering Ask Lini, Risk Detector, Document Summarization, Minute Generation, and every AI capability across the suite. 
We are building a dedicated squad around it and are looking for a strong Software / Product Engineer, with a focus our platform architecture, to help us bring it to the next level. 


As a Software Engineer work at the intersection of AI, product, and engineering. You will contribute to building, improving, and scaling the features that make Lini a reliable and powerful AI layer across the entire DiliTrust suite. 


We are looking for an engineer who writes clean, production-ready code and is comfortable taking ownership of features end-to-end, from technical design to deployment. We also care about how you think about AI: whether you bring genuine curiosity to the product, and whether you can translate a model capability into a great user experience. 


Missions

Write specifications as the durable asset of the project. Executable acceptance criteria, and — crucially — the non-functional requirements that specs almost never carry: data classification, endpoint × role authorization matrix, volumetry assumptions, latency and throughput budgets. These are the requirements whose later correction is superlinear, so they get decided before generation, not after.
Freeze the contracts before any fan-out. API schemas, types, module boundaries, invariants. Agents do not negotiate an interface in the hallway: each will make a plausible and incompatible assumption, discovered at integration.
Pilot coding agents with a tight brief and a bounded context — narrow tasks, defined input and output artifacts, explicit stop conditions and budgets, full traceability of what produced each change.
Keep producer and verifier separate. You do not sign off alone on generation you piloted, and you act as independent verifier on your peers' slices — with an adversarial brief ("find what breaks against this spec"), never "confirm this looks fine".
Build the asymmetric gates that make the slice safe at volume — expensive to satisfy, cheap to check: property tests, contract tests, query-count and allocation budgets, execution-plan checks, policy-as-code, backward-compatibility proofs. Written before the implementation exists, so the agent closes the feedback loop itself without consuming human attention.
Use code reading as a calibration instrument, not as a gate. Sample deliberately, by risk zone, to measure the real defect rate of the generator-plus-gates pair and to keep the team's mental model of its own system alive.
Keep work-in-progress low. Capped PR size, thin vertical slices, trunk-based with very short branches, feature flags over long-lived branches, CI as the agent's first task rather than its last. More features in flight does not mean faster delivery when the bottleneck is verification.
Design for blast radius. Reversibility, progressive delivery, structured logs, traces, metrics and instrumentation generated as a matter of course. On many paths, detecting in five minutes beats three days of review that prevents nothing.


Requirements
Being based in France with full working rights. Fluent in French and English.
Experience & Seniority:

8+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a significant portion spent building and operating B2B SaaS platforms in production
Proven ownership of features across their full lifecycle — design, delivery, iteration, maintenance — on long-lived, multi-year products
Strong background in complex, scalable web architectures, including real modularity: you have seen where coupling stops parallel work dead

AI-Native Practice:

Demonstrated, sustained use of coding agents in production work — not autocomplete, but delegated implementation with review and accountability
A concrete, articulated view of where generated code fails: correlated defects rather than idiosyncratic ones, uniform surface quality that destroys the usual "look here" review signals, plausibility with no author to interrogate
Comfort being accountable for code you did not author, and the discipline to refuse a change you cannot explain

Verification & Quality:

Real fluency in property-based testing, contract testing, and deriving tests from the specification rather than from the code
Test-data strategy, including maintaining a volumetrically representative dataset as part of the verification apparatus — not a nice-to-have
Instinct for the difference between a rigorous check and a scalable one: does the cost of checking grow with the volume produced?

Security & Performance (non-negotiable on this role):

Authorization modelling in multi-tenant systems, and why declarative, centrally enforced authorization beats reviewing each endpoint. Generated code reliably checks who you are and regularly forgets whether you are allowed
Awareness of the attack surface specific to an agent-assisted pipeline: prompt injection through ticket descriptions, code comments and dependency READMEs; supply-chain risk on hallucinated package names; least privilege for non-human identities; and the most frequent risk of all — production data or proprietary code leaking into the development loop
Performance as a measured number rather than a code-reading opinion: query budgets per HTTP request, N+1, unbounded result sets, missing indexes on new query paths, network calls in loops, execution-plan review. These are invisible at test-data scale and expensive in production

Product & Team Collaboration:

Excellent written communication — specification writing is now a core engineering skill on this role, not documentation overhead
Extensive experience working directly with product managers, designers and stakeholders in a product-oriented setup
Strong sense of ownership and sound judgment on risk: what to build, what not to build, what residual risk is acceptable and why

Education:

Master's degree in Engineering or equivalent practical experience in senior SaaS environments


What this role is not
We would rather say it up front:

It is not a prompt-engineering role, and it is not an ML/LLM research role.
It is not a role where green tests are sufficient evidence. On security and performance, "the spec is met and the tests pass" is not a weak signal — it is a null one.
It is not a ticket queue. The profile that shrinks in an AI-native team is the one whose value was implementing assigned tickets between two boundaries.


Our Tech Stack

Backend: Node.js / TypeScript
Frontend: Vue.js 3
Database: PostgreSQL, MariaDB
DevOps: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform
Cloud: GCP

Engineering apparatus you will use and help build: coding agents orchestrated deterministically in CI, aspect-scoped verification agents (authorization, performance, spec conformance, dependencies), policy-as-code, property-based and contract testing, volumetric test datasets, load and endurance gates on critical paths, feature flags, progressive delivery and end-to-end tracing.

What we offer

Join a fast-growing company in a friendly, international environment — engineering primarily in Paris, with further engineering presence in Berlin, Montreal and Wilmington (DE), and offices across France, Italy, Spain, Germany, Canada, the USA, Mexico and Dubai;
Our "Remote Policy" guarantees that you can find the right balance between "Onsite" and "Remote";
Last but not least, all the day-to-day benefits of the CSE, luncheon vouchers, profit sharing bonuses, etc...
